_comment: did_v1 -> V_eta migration TARGET map: for each v1 source class, the V_eta document class(es) its migrator actually emits. targets = pass-1 emitted classes; carried = pre-existing classes attached to (not minted); second_pass = classes minted in the NDI second pass; decided_targets = a signed decision no migrator implements yet; confirmed_targets = the team read what the migrator ALREADY emits and accepted it as the end state (the opposite of decided_targets -- never merge them); how = one-line authored intent; flags = caveats (dynamic emit, header/code mismatch, deferrals). Consumed by tools/coverage.py to fill the ledger's target column. == targets IS GENERATED, THE REST IS AUTHORED. Re-run `python3 tools/refresh_migration_targets.py` after any migrator change; `--check` fails when it is stale. It follows the call graph from each class's entry point in +migrators_j (falling back to +migrators, which is where V_eta lands when +migrators_j has no file) through private/ helpers and local subfunctions, resolving class names passed as parameters at their call sites, and reuses tools/status_board.py's statement-level extractor so a `superclasses` entry is never read as a document class. It rewrites a row only when every reachable emission resolved; where one did not (element, measurement, ontology_table_row, subjectmeasurement -- all pick their leaf class at runtime) the row can only GAIN, never lose. A migrator that mints nothing keeps a target naming ITSELF and loses any target naming another class. == ON session_relative_reference, WHICH IS A CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO COMMITTED RECORDS AND IS NOT RESOLVED HERE. 36 rows name `session_relative_reference`, because private/jSessionAnchor.m:19 mints it and every observation migrator calls that helper. The signed time model (V_eta_time_reference_model_plan.md) COLLAPSES it, with seven siblings, into `relative_reference`. Both are true of different moments, and both halves are already in the code: private/jEpochClockReferences.m:141 and private/jClockAlignmentBodies.m:174 mint `relative_reference` today, which is why 4 rows name the new class while 36 name the old one. So a `session_relative_reference` target is a statement about what pass 1 EMITS TODAY, never a decision that the class survives; the decision is the sign-off in the plan document, and tools/status_board.py's RETIRED_BY_ITS_OWN_DECISION carries the same reading. Rewriting the 36 rows to a class their migrators do not emit would make this file describe an intention rather than the code.

unread_targets.why: AUTHORED, because `targets` is DERIVED and this tool cannot derive these. element.m:118 calls private/jRecordingObservation, whose construction site is `classBlock(e.class, ...)` at :209 -- a VARIABLE. The literals are three steps away, in private/jRecordingModality.m, passed to a local helper `mk` and returned as a struct field: `mk('voltage_observation', ...)` at :190, :198, :208, :218, plus current_observation :200/:209, image_observation :214, acceleration_observation :220, temperature_observation :222 -- five distinct classes over eight sites. Following that is inter-procedural data flow through a struct field across two files, which the derivation deliberately does not attempt; it reports the site instead (see `target_completeness`). THE EMISSION IS NOT IN DOUBT: this is the SIGNED raw-recording observation (V_eta_recording_observation_plan.md:99, 2026-08-10), it is what carries `instrument_id`, and NDI-matlab's PRED end-to-end test asserts the `voltage_observation` it produces (TestMigrateLocalEtaPRED, run 31748129747, 8/8). Only ONE of the five is corpus-exercised -- PRED is an ephys corpus -- so the other four are recorded as REACHABLE from the table, not as observed.

oneepoch.how: KEEPS ITS CLASS -- a block FOLD, not a dissolution. `oneepoch` is the record of a CONCATENATION (ndi.element.oneepoch glues an element's N epochs into one); its only own field, `epoch_ids`, is the comma-joined list of the sources. Everything else arrives by inheritance from `element_epoch`, which V_eta renames to `acquisition_epoch` -- so no class of that name exists to inherit from and the inherited block would trip the strict top-level check (did2:validation:undeclaredBlock). The migrator moves that block's contents onto the `oneepoch` block and drops the shell. Field-by-field, so an unrecognised v1 field surfaces as undeclaredField rather than riding along unvalidated.
oneepoch.flags: PASSTHROUGH REPAIR, NOT THE MODEL. Before this the class had NO V_eta schema at all -- coverage.py tagged it non-production, which suppressed the gap -- and a real document quarantined on `No schema file for class "oneepoch"` (measured: DID-matlab scratch probe 8, run 31423494433). The go-forward model is fork A1, chosen by the team 2026-08-10 and recorded in V_eta_epoch_plan.md: the concatenation becomes a typed observation whose `derived_from_#` edges point at the N per-epoch observations, and NO `epoch` entity is minted for the synthetic `whole_session_<ref>` id. That build is gated on the raw-recording plan being signed. NOTE the tombstone declares `clocks`, NOT the did_v1 `epoch_clock`/`t0_t1`: the base element_epoch superclass migrator collapses the pair before validation sees the document, so the did_v1 names never arrive.

Nothing converts until a team call names a home for it" -- true when written, and contradicted by its own `targets` the moment the edge landed, because refresh_migration_targets.py owns `targets` and says in its own words that this prose is not touched by it. The team call was made (option A): `acquisition_system` gains a SECOND software edge, `software_id -> software`, optional, and the guard in migrators_j/daqsystem.m is DELETED. `ndi_daqsystem_class` ('ndi.daq.system.mfdaq' / '.image') now folds to a `software` entity through jSoftware, the same route its three siblings take -- it is the OBJECT-RECONSTRUCTION KEY read by ndi_document2ndi_object via a CONSTRUCTED field name, which is why a literal grep called it dead. The edge is OPTIONAL because NDI's template sets no mustbenotempty and jSoftware returns [] for an empty name, so the no-software path is real; #37 is armed, so a required edge here would quarantine those documents. EXPECTED CORPUS MOVEMENT, none of it measured here: `unconverted_by_class.daqsystem` -> 0; `acquisition_system` appears on real data for the first time; and the TOTAL document count RISES, because this is now a 1->2 fold. valid_interval.how: NO PASS-1 MIGRATOR, deliberately: the document passes through under its own tombstone (the identity migrator), which is what stops it stranding. THE SECOND PASS IS DORMANT AS OF 2026-08-12 AND EMITS NOTHING -- team decision (jess@walthamdatascience.com): the model is ONE statement per source document carrying an ARRAY of booleans against a TIME AXIS, and the team chose to WAIT for `axes[]` (#45, blocked on #32) rather than ship the 1->N one-statement-per-interval decomposition as an interim step. So `valid_interval` documents live on their v1 tombstone today and nothing downstream of them exists yet. `did2.convert.resolveValidIntervals` still RUNS as a census (`sources_seen` / `intervals_seen` measure the deferred work) and its decomposition logic is preserved behind `options.Decompose`, default FALSE. WHEN IT IS RE-ARMED the class it emits is `logical_observation` (renamed from `validity_observation` on 2026-08-12: the 32 `*_observation` data_types name a KIND OF VALUE and the SEMANTIC belongs in `subject_statement.variable`), plus the `relative_reference` each statement is anchored to (start = t0, duration = t1 - t0, clock de-encoded from clocktypestring). A batch pass and not a migrator for the same structural reason as resolveSessionAnchors: `relative_reference.relative_to` is REQUIRED and names the `epoch` DOCUMENT, whose id exists only after did2.convert.epochMint has minted it corpus-wide, and a single-document migrator holds an epoch STRING it cannot map to a document id.
valid_interval.flags: ADDS, NEVER REMOVES -- and while DORMANT it adds nothing at all. The source document is KEPT under its v1 tombstone (nothing required, `element_id` optional), so a passthrough cannot trip mustBeNonEmpty or undeclaredField. NOT SIGNED: no TEAM-SIGN-OFF line exists, so the board keeps rendering this family as awaiting review. The 2026-08-11 'decision' was a QUESTION recorded as an answer (#103); the 2026-08-12 decisions are (a) the ARRAY model with a time axis is the target and (b) the classes are named `logical` / `logical_observation`, not `validity` / `validity_observation`. `sequence` is DELETED: v1's array-append order is invisible to its only consumer (tuning_response.m:253-256 indexes identifyvalidintervals's RETURN VALUE, and markgarbage.m:178-204 accumulates every row through a set union without indexing by position). OPEN SUB-QUESTION, deliberately not pre-empted: NDI's loadvalidinterval inherits a derived element's validity from its `underlying_element` (markgarbage.m:146-155), and whether V_eta re-derives that at query time or materialises it is a team call -- both remain buildable.
